title: LLM Behavior & Safety Escalation Matrix and Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines the triage, escalation matrix, and operational runbook for customer-facing incidents caused by LLM behavior or safety failures (e.g., hallucinations with high customer impact, PII leakage, prompt-injection exploits, toxic output). It is written for customer-success managers, SRE/oncall engineers, product safety owners, and account teams to ensure consistent, fast, and auditable responses.

Scope and intended use
---------------------
- Applies to incidents where a Redwood-hosted or Dedicated/Private tenant experiences correctable or unbounded LLM output risks that affect customer business, compliance, or safety.
- Excludes purely internal model training failures; those are covered by the Applied-ML team runbooks.
- Use during on-call incidents, QBR escalations, or executive-facing customer communications.

Definitions and incident types
------------------------------
- Severity P0 (Critical): confirmed PII/data exfiltration, regulatory exposure, or sustained harmful content generation to multiple end-users. Immediate business or legal risk.
- Severity P1 (High): reproducible toxic or incorrect outputs that materially degrade customer experience or violate policy but limited scope.
- Severity P2 (Medium): single-tenant unexpected behavior with mitigations available, non-urgent.
- Severity P3 (Low): minor quality regressions, intermittent anomalies, or non-customer-impacting model drift.

Escalation matrix (summary)
--------------------------
- P0: Immediate escalation to Customer Success Lead -> SRE Pager -> Product Safety Oncall -> Legal & Security notified. Exec update within 2 hours.
- P1: Customer Success -> Product Manager -> Runtime Engineering oncall. External customer update within 4 hours.
- P2: Customer Success -> Technical Account Manager -> Assigned Eng owner. Resolution target 72 hours.
- P3: Logged as a ticket, triaged during weekly ops cadence.

Severity mapping and responsibilities (table)
--------------------------------------------
- Columns: Severity | First Responder | Engineering Ownership | Communication SLA | Temporary Mitigation
- P0 | Customer Success oncall or Account TPM | SRE Pager + Product Safety | 2 hours (initial) | Immediate model switch/traffic quarantine + disable streaming
- P1 | Customer Success SE | Runtime Eng oncall | 4 hours | Canary rollback or throttled requests
- P2 | TAM | Assigned Eng | 72 hours | Enable conservative decoding profile
- P3 | Support queue | Product QA | 2 weeks | Monitor & collect repros

Initial triage checklist (first 30 mins)
--------------------------------------
1. Confirm incident scope: affected tenants, API keys, model versions, routes.
2. Capture reproducible example(s) and timestamps. Preserve request IDs and tenant IDs.
3. Take quick mitigation: enable safe-fallback route, revoke temporary API key if compromised, or enable content-filtering middleware.
4. Assign severity using definitions above and page the appropriate oncall roles.
5. Notify customer contact with an acknowledgement note (template below) and expected update window.

Required telemetry & artifacts
-----------------------------
- Request IDs and raw request/response payload (scrub PII if storing externally).
- Model config snapshot: model name, quantization profile, decoding strategy, temperature/top_p, runtime kernels.
- Ingress/egress telemetry: request latency, token counts, error rates in last 24 hours.
- Replay token streams (KV cache traces) when available.
- SIEM/IDS evidence for injection vectors.

Immediate mitigation recipes (playbook-style)
--------------------------------------------
- Quarantine tenant traffic (SRE step): update routing policy to divert 100% of the tenant to an isolated pool with enhanced filtering. Command (example):
  - kubectl patch configmap ingress-policy -p '{"data":{"tenant-123":"quarantine"}}'
- Model switch (Product Safety / Runtime): switch route to verified-safe model variant (e.g., redwood/gptx-safe-1-v2) and set decoding profile to conservative. CLI: redwoodctl route update --tenant TENANT --model gptx-safe-1-v2 --decoding conservative
- Disable streaming tokens: lower blast radius for partial outputs.
- Rate-limit or backpressure: if abuse suspected, reduce rps quota to 0.1x for the tenant.

Communication templates
-----------------------
- Acknowledgement (first contact):
  "Hello <customer_contact>, we have received your report and are actively investigating. We have temporarily routed your requests to a safety-protected variant and will provide an update within <X hours>. Reference: <INCIDENT-ID>."
- Update (post-triage):
  "Root cause hypothesis: <short>. Mitigation applied: <action>. Next steps: <investigation steps and ETA>."

Root cause investigation playbook (24–72 hours)
----------------------------------------------
1. Reproduce with recorded inputs in a safe sandbox. Note whether problem is deterministic or stochastic.
2. Compare outputs across model versions and decoding configurations.
3. Review recent model rollouts and telemetry for correlated drift signals.
4. Conduct log correlation with ingress gateway and WAF logs for injection patterns.
5. If PII exposure suspected, notify Security & Legal and begin evidence preservation per the Data Incident runbook.

Rollback and remediation criteria
--------------------------------
- Remediation (safe to restore normal routing) requires: no reproduction in 24h under controlled load, red-team fuzzing shows failure rate <0.01%, and customer verification.
- If remediation cannot be validated within SLA, keep tenant on conservative routing and schedule a patch release with Product Safety priority.

Post-incident steps and customer QBR integration
-----------------------------------------------
- Owner creates a postmortem within 72 hours including timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, and recommended product/process changes.
- Customer Success will include the incident in the next QBR, with an action plan and acceptance criteria for closure.
- Track regressions in the model onboarding/evals system and attach the failing prompt-sets to the customer record.

Drills and readiness
-------------------
- Run an LLM-behavior game day quarterly with customer-success, SRE, and Product Safety.
- Synthetic scenarios: PII leak, targeted prompt injection, and surge of toxic outputs.
- Success criteria: mean acknowledgement <= 30 minutes, mitigation applied <= 60 minutes, restoration decision <= 24 hours.

Roles and contacts (oncall responsibilities)
-------------------------------------------
- Customer Success Lead: overall customer comms and executive updates.
- Technical Account Manager (TAM): coordinates technical remediation with customer.
- SRE oncall: executes routing changes, throttles, and tenant quarantines.
- Product Safety oncall: determines model-level mitigations, decoding profiles, and rollout holds.
- Legal & Security: engaged for PII/regulatory incidents.

Appendix A: SIEM & query examples
--------------------------------
- Example: find requests with inline user-provided prompt-hints matching regex: /execute\s+command|curl\s+http/ in last 6 hours.
- Example CloudWatch filter: { $.responseText = "*password*" } | display @timestamp, requestId, tenantId

Appendix B: Email and slack templates (short)
---------------------------------------------
- Slack incident channel pinned message: "INCIDENT-<ID> | Severity: P0 | Status: Investigating | Owners: CS/Aisha,Pg-SRE/Oncall"
- Executive summary email subject: "[INCIDENT-<ID>] P0 LLM Behavior — Immediate Actions and Next Steps"
